verses.text: These are King Lemuel's words, the revelation his mother taught him.
“Oh, my son! The son I carried! The son I made vows for!
Don't spend your strength chasing women or live in ways that bring kings down.
Lemuel, wine isn't for kings. Rulers shouldn't be asking, ‘Where's the strong stuff?’
They might drink, forget the law, and twist the justice owed to someone who's suffering.
Give strong drink to the person who's about to die, and wine to those bitter with grief.
Let them drink and forget how poor they are, and stop remembering their misery.
Speak up for people who can't speak, and take up the case of everyone who's been left with nobody.
Open your mouth, judge fairly, and make sure poor and needy people get justice.”
Who can find a woman of real character? She's worth far more than rubies.
Her husband trusts her with his whole heart. He'll have everything he needs to prosper.
She does him good and never harm, all the days of her life.
She goes looking for wool and flax and gets right to work with her hands.
She's like a fleet of merchant ships, bringing food home from far away.
She gets up while it's still dark and gives her household food, with portions for her servant girls.
She checks out a field and buys it. With what her own hands earned, she plants a vineyard.
She gets herself ready for hard work and makes her arms strong.
She sees that what she sells turns a profit. Her lamp is still burning at night.
She reaches for the distaff and takes hold of the spindle.
She opens her arms to poor people and reaches out to anyone in need.
Snow doesn't scare her on account of her household. Everybody at home is dressed in scarlet.
She makes her own woven coverings. She wears fine linen and purple.
Her husband is respected at the city gates, where he sits with the elders of the land.
She makes linen clothes to sell and supplies the merchant with sashes.
She wears strength and dignity like clothes and laughs at the days ahead.
When she speaks, wisdom comes out. She teaches with kindness.
She keeps an eye on how things go at home and never sits around eating the bread of idleness.
Her children stand up and call her blessed. Her husband praises her too.
“Lots of women do noble things, but you've gone above them all.”
Charm can fool you, and beauty won't last. A woman who stands in awe of the LORD deserves praise.
Give her what her hands have earned! Let the work she's done speak her praise at the city gates!
